morphosyntactic_inflection_agreement.rule: Japanese verbs and adjectives NEVER agree with the subject in grammatical person (1st, 2nd, 3rd), grammatical number (singular, plural), or grammatical gender (masculine, feminine, neuter).

proof.first_person_singular: 私は本を読む (watashi wa hon o yomu)
proof.second_person_plural: あなたたちは本を読む (anatatachi wa hon o yomu)
proof.third_person_singular: 彼は本を読む (kare wa hon o yomu)

honorific_concord.rule: In Japanese, 'agreement' is social concord: the predicate honorific form must strictly concord with the relative social rank and in-group/out-group status of the referent and interlocutor.

dimensions.subject_elevation_sonkeigo: If subject is superior/out-group, verb must take Sonkeigo (先生がいらっしゃる / 社長がおっしゃる).
dimensions.self_lowering_kenjougo: If subject is speaker/in-group directing action toward superior, verb must take Kenjougo (私が伺う / 私が申し上げる).
